transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Eleanor Park (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Tom Wu (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Polaris PM), Jorge Alvarez (Polaris Infra), Lena Park (Polaris ML)

Summary: quick hosted api demo covering chat/text generation basics with emphasis on streaming, params, and retry behavior.

00:00 - Eleanor: hey everyone thanks for joining from redwood, um we're excited to walk through the hosted api today, quick round of intros?
00:22 - Maya: hi im maya product here, exploring a chat assistant for our ecom storefront, main goals faster answers and some personalization, uh low latency for quick follow ups
00:37 - Jorge: jorge infra, we'll be evaluating from an infra and risk perspective, data retention and sso are big for us
00:52 - Eleanor: great, i'll hand off to samir for the demo flow and then tom will show console and optimize suggestions
01:10 - Samir: cool thanks, so plan is: api basics, streaming demo, request params (temp, tokens), retry semantics, then console quick tour, any must-see items from you maya?
01:28 - Maya: curious about streaming and partial tokens - can we stream incremental responses to reduce perceived latency?
01:45 - Samir: yeah absolutely, we support server-sent events and chunked streaming, you get partial tokens as they generate so UI can show first word fast; caveat, you need to handle rubrics for truncation and incremental content merging
02:10 - Lena: is there SDK support in js/python for streaming? sometimes our front end team prefers websocket approach
02:22 - Samir: we have official SDKs in js/python, examples for sse and chunked responses. websocket is possible via the gateway but sse is easiest for web clients; i'll share code snippets
02:40 - Tom: jumping in, on the console we also show token-level timing so you can see where latency is spent which helps tune batching and prompt size
03:05 - Jorge: how about param tuning — like temperature, top_p, max_tokens — what's common for short assistant replies?
03:20 - Samir: for deterministic replies stick to temp 0-0.3, top_p 0.8-1.0, max_tokens depends on expected length; we showed a few profiles in the catalog, and the model variant matters too - some open models are cheaper but less consistent
03:40 - Maya: cost vs latency tradeoff — if we need sub-300ms 1-turn replies for SKU lookup, do we need dedicated?
04:00 - Eleanor: depends on your QPS and SLOs; hosted can hit low latency for spiky workloads but dedicated reserved capacity gives more predictable p95; for sub-300ms you might evaluate with a small dedicated pool or a tuned hosted route to a low-latency model variant
04:28 - Jorge: what about retries? if a request times out, how do we avoid double charges / duplicate actions?
04:40 - Samir: good question. we recommend idempotency keys on create-like requests; for generation calls we expose a request_id and you can re-use the same input to rehydrate from cache if within KV cache TTL. Also retries should use exponential backoff and detect partial-stream responses — server will return a final id when generation completes
05:10 - Maya: partial-stream detection sounds tricky — any SDK helpers?
05:20 - Samir: yes our SDKs surface events: chunk, done, error; done includes final token counts and request_id. For client side, you should handle the done event to mark completion and avoid re-sending the same id
05:45 - Tom: i'll demo the console, opening the token trace for a short chat session, note the prefix cache hit on system prompt which saved about 30% tokens in this example
06:10 - [screen share noise, background typing]
06:30 - Tom: here in the console you can toggle streaming vs non-streaming, and see per-token latency bar, you can also drill into per-route cost estimates and set a max tokens guardrail
06:55 - Maya: can we set per-route quotas? we want to limit dev/test traffic and spike protect prod
07:10 - Eleanor: yes per-route quotas, rate-limits and per-key usage breakdowns, plus alerting in console; if you need hard isolation that's where dedicated comes in
07:35 - Jorge: security questions — do you support SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logs, and data residency?
07:50 - Eleanor: yes we support SSO, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments, and hosted customers get audit logs and retention controls; we'll attach SOC2 and ISO cert summaries in the security packet
08:18 - Maya: what's default data retention for hosted logs?
08:25 - Eleanor: default is 30 days for logs, and you can configure longer retention or purge policies; for strict regs we'd recommend Private with a customer-managed plane
08:40 - Lena: ok back to streaming — whats the cost model? are we charged per partial chunk?
08:52 - Samir: charges are token based at final token counts, we only bill on final output tokens generated plus input tokens; intermediate stream chunks don't incur additional billing beyond final token calculation
09:10 - Maya: if we do partial prefix caching across turns, how does caching interact with billing?
09:22 - Samir: prefix caching reduces input token size because you can reuse system prompt in cache keyed by conversation id — billing still counts tokens sent/returned but cache reduces tokens needed to send each request so lowers bill
09:45 - Tom: quick demo of retry: i'll simulate a transient 503 and show the sdk backoff behavior, notice it will reattempt with exponential backoff and the client gets the same request_id on final success
10:10 - [simulated error noise]
10:25 - Tom: here you see the sdk retries 3 times then succeeds, console shows the retry attempts and final timing, we also instrument partial stream so you can see whether a previous attempt returned chunks
10:50 - Jorge: are there any guarantees on replay — like if a user sees a partial answer and clicks send again?
11:00 - Samir: generally treat generation as non-idempotent unless you use deterministic settings (temp 0) and idempotency tokens; for actions that mutate external state use separate idempotent endpoints
11:20 - Maya: curious about model catalog — can we pick specific variants for lower latency vs higher quality?
11:30 - Samir: yes we expose model variants and performance profiles; catalog includes a 'low-latency' label and 'high-quality' label, and the smart routing can fall back to cheaper variants when congested
11:50 - Maya: how do we measure quality regressions during rollouts?
12:00 - Eleanor: we include eval hooks and you can upload prompt sets; the platform runs A/B and regression checks and notifies on quality drops. Optimize suggests quantization or batching configs for cost wins while observing eval metrics
12:30 - Lena: about batching — our workload is bursty, will batching increase latency too much?
12:42 - Samir: batching helps throughput and lowers unit cost but increases tail latency for single-turn p99; our runtime supports micro-batching and priority routing to protect low-latency requests
13:05 - Maya: can you demo a short chat with streaming turned on?
13:12 - Samir: sure hitting the hosted endpoint now, sending a product question prompt, streaming on —
13:25 - [short stream playback with partial tokens visible]
13:40 - Maya: ok that looks clean, can we abort streams from client?
13:48 - Samir: yes you can close the connection; server will mark request aborted and you can opt to not bill for aborted requests if no tokens were finalized — there are specifics, we'll include docs
14:05 - Jorge: what about concurrency — what if we have 200 concurrent users, how does hosted handle bursts?
14:18 - Eleanor: hosted autoscaling handles spikes but if you have predictable high concurrency, dedicated reserved pools give capacity guarantees; for mixed traffic use smart routing and priority tiers
14:40 - Maya: can we set SLA on p95 latency?
14:48 - Eleanor: hosted has best-effort p95 targets; dedicated has SLA options in reserved contracts, also you can set latency-based routing policies to prefer low-latency nodes
15:05 - Tom: switching to the console: here's a sample Optimize suggestion — it noticed repeated system prompts and suggested prefix caching which saved tokens, and also recommended a lower-precision quant profile for this workload to cut GPU cost 20% with minor quality regression
15:40 - Lena: is quantization applied in hosted or only on dedicated/private runtimes?
15:48 - Samir: quantization profiles are currently in dedicated/private for now but we're piloting some lightweight quant transforms in hosted; optimize will flag recommendations either way
16:05 - Maya: about rollout strategies — can we canary a new model?
16:12 - Eleanor: yes you can do canary by route, A/B traffic splits, and automatic rollback if eval metrics cross thresholds
16:30 - Jorge: do you support network egress restrictions? we need to enforce VPC egress rules in our environment
16:45 - Eleanor: hosted can't lock egress to your VPC, that's where Private comes in; for hosted we support VPC peering and private links in some regions, but not full egress control
17:05 - Maya: ok budget question — whats typical for 100k messages per month?
17:15 - Samir: depends on average tokens per message; with 20 input + 40 output tokens at hosted rates, rough math gives X dollars — i'll send a worked example in the pricing sheet. We also showed Optimize suggestions that could reduce per-message cost via caching and smaller variants
17:45 - Tom: quick regs note — we'll attach SOC2/ISO docs and a short notes sheet on KMS integrations; dedicated/private options have different contractual terms
18:10 - Maya: anything else for security? logging, masking PII?
18:20 - Eleanor: we provide redaction hooks and can setup PII masking at ingestion; also audit logs for who accessed what and retention controls
18:45 - Maya: timeline — we're hoping to run a 2-week POC in late feb if things look good
18:55 - Eleanor: great, we'll target provisioning trial keys this week, run a benchmark with your traffic sample, and then discuss Dedicated quotes if the POC passes
19:10 - [wrap up and final clarifications]
19:30 - Eleanor: recap: i'll send pricing and security packet, samir will provision keys and sample scripts, lena will upload prompts, polaris to share traffic shape, schedule benchmark next week
19:55 - Maya: thanks team really helpful, looking forward to the trial
20:10 - Jorge: thanks all, bye

End transcript.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings and punctuation inconsistencies as typical for automated captions. References to "Optimize" and "Console" are Redwood product terms; 'quantization' and 'KV cache' may appear abbreviated or slightly mis-transcribed.
